findings.title: Legacy PATCH/nested-PUT clients now silently hide the group and get a success response
findings.body:
The PATCH path (`changes: {add:, delete:}`) and the nested `group: {...}` payload were removed, but `resources :groups` still routes PATCH and PUT to `update`.

An existing API client that sends `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes[add]=bob` now reaches `update`, where:
- `params[:visible]` is nil, so `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` sets the group to invisible;
- no members are added;
- the response is `success_json`.

A PUT with the old nested `group[usernames]` / `group[visible]` format behaves the same way.

Integrations such as SSO/group-sync scripts would believe the membership change succeeded while the group was actually hidden. Either keep backward compatibility or reject unknown or legacy payloads explicitly, and only assign `visible` when the param is present.

findings.title: remove_member bypasses Group#remove and GroupUser destroy callbacks
findings.body:
`group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association deletes the `group_users` join rows with `delete_all`. No `GroupUser` callbacks run, and the model's own `Group#remove(user)` logic is skipped; the previous incremental-delete code called `group.remove(user)`.

This is also asymmetric with `add_members`, which uses `group.add(user)`. Any cleanup tied to membership removal (destroy callbacks, primary-group or title cleanup, counters) will not happen.

If `user_id` is not a member, `find` raises `RecordNotFound` instead of returning a clear error. Look up the user and call `group.remove(user)` instead.

findings.title: Adding a user who is already a member raises; partial adds and silent UI failure
findings.body:
`group.add(user)` does `users.push(user)` with no membership check. For an existing member this violates the unique `group_users(group_id, user_id)` constraint (or validation) and raises, producing a 500. Users earlier in the comma list stay added because there is no transaction.

This is now the main admin UI path, and the UI makes it easy to hit:
- `addMembers` in admin-group.js.es6 does not clear the input after a successful add (TODO noted), so clicking Add twice re-submits the same usernames.
- `Group#addMembers` has no rejection handler, so the admin sees nothing.

Skip users who are already members, e.g. `group.add(user) unless group.users.include?(user)`, and surface errors in the client.

findings.title: totalPages off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With exactly 50 members and a limit of 50 it reports 2 pages.

On page 1, `showingLast` is false, so the "next" control is enabled. Clicking it sets offset to 50, fetches an empty member list, and shows "2/2" with no members. The same happens for 100, 150, and so on.

Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Public group members page now truncates at 50 members with no way to page
findings.body:
`members` now defaults to `limit = 50` for every group; previously non-automatic groups returned all members. The public `group-members` route calls `model.findMembers()` with the default limit and offset 0.

`templates/group/members.hbs` has no next/previous controls, so any group with more than 50 members shows only the first 50 on its public page, and the rest cannot be reached. Add pagination or infinite loading to the public page, or keep the old behaviour there.

findings.title: Breaking change in /groups/:id/members.json response shape
findings.body:
The endpoint used to return a bare JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}` and is paginated by default.

Any external consumer of this public endpoint will break: iterating the response, or expecting the full member list for non-automatic groups. Other client code that calls `findMembers()` expecting a promise of an array will also break, because the method now resolves to undefined and only mutates the model.

This should be called out or versioned, and any remaining callers audited.

findings.title: limit/offset not validated or clamped
findings.body:
`limit` and `offset` come straight from `to_i`.
- A negative value makes PostgreSQL raise ("LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative"), giving a 500.
- `limit=0` is echoed back in `meta.limit`, and the admin controller then divides by it in `currentPage`/`totalPages`, producing NaN/Infinity.
- Arbitrarily large limits are accepted on this publicly reachable endpoint.

Clamp `limit` to a sane range, e.g. 1..200, and `offset` to >= 0.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The new flattened `asJSON` sends `alias_level` on POST, and the form exposes the alias-level combo box before the group exists. `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`, so the alias level chosen when creating a group is silently dropped until the admin saves again.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb and relies on seeded id 1
findings.body:
The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" example issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members"`. Controller specs do not enforce the verb, so the test passes without exercising the real request.

Several examples (`add_members`, `remove_member`, `update`) also assume `Group.find(1)` exists and is automatic, which depends on seed data. Fabricate an automatic group explicitly and use `:delete`.

findings.title: No coverage for the new paginated members endpoint or normal-group update
findings.body:
`GroupsController#members` changed its response format and added limit/offset pagination, but no spec covers the new `members`/`meta` structure or the pagination behaviour.

The `.update` context only tests that a rename is ignored on an automatic group. Renaming a normal group and changing `alias_level` are untested, as is the removal of the PATCH path (no test asserts how legacy PATCH requests are handled).
